transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Start: 10:30 AM PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Natarajan (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood Partner Ops), Dana Morales (ClearData Head of Partnerships), Ethan Wu (ClearData Platform Sales), Laila Ahmed (ClearData CISO), Tom Reyes (ClearData Cloud Architect)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be incomplete): Quick alignment on co-sell play, pilot accounts, and security gating. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a saturday morning, appreciate it. quick agenda — partner GTM motion, pilot scope, timeline, then technical constraints. Marcus's going to jump into the performance bits.
[00:22] Dana: thanks priya. saturday? actually monday for me, so good. we wanted to make sure we had the revenue split discussion up front since our rev ops needs to map it out.
[00:38] Priya: totally. high level we usually run a co-sell where the partner gets referral fee + reseller markup for Dedicated and a different split for hosted. janelle will cover the ops side.
[00:52] Janelle: my ask is to keep the contract simple — we don't want double-billing for pilot. also need a clause about lead ownership and handover timeline.
[01:10] Ethan: and to be concrete — our AMs want clarity on pricing tiers before we talk to the first three pilot accounts.
[01:22] Marcus: okay i'll flag that for the bench. for the pilot we'll propose two configurations: Redwood-hosted with region pinning (US-EAST) and Redwood Dedicated pool on ClearData's GCP project — small footprint to start.
[01:45] Tom: quick interjection — when you say dedicated on our GCP, do you mean customer-managed VPC with a private deployment or a dedicated tenant managed by Redwood?
[02:02] Marcus: good question. there's two flavors. for Dedicated we can run in a Redwood-managed reserved capacity but with network peering and private endpoints — or Private deployment where ClearData hosts the control plane in your VPC. for the pilot we recommend reserved Dedicated with strict egress rules, unless you insist on full Private.
[02:27] Laila: security is our main blocker. SOC2 is fine but we need to see KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention for 7 years, and data residency controls. also SSO/SAML integration for RBAC.
[02:50] Priya: understood. we'll share our SOC2 cert and the audit log retention options. quick note — our audit log naming in the docs sometimes shows product name 'Redwood Infr' in older exports, so apologies for mismatch.
[03:06] Dana: ha, yeah we saw that. small note: our legal hates product name inconsistencies.
[03:18] Marcus: back to the tech — latency targets from ClearData pilot accounts? what would success look like?
[03:28] Ethan: sub-200ms p95 for completion for short prompts; for embeddings batch throughput we care about tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, and model mismatch risk.
[03:44] Marcus: got it. for hosted we can show p95 of ~150-220ms on our side depending on model and seq length. for dedicated with colocated GPUs we can push p95 to ~80-120ms but with extra run cost. these numbers are approximate — need a micro-benchmark with your payloads.
[04:05] Tom: payloads — we have chat + document search embeddings, avg seq 120 tokens for generation, embedding batches of 512 items. also some longer format reranking flows.
[04:20] Marcus: that helps. we'll configure a representative workload: gen seq 120 tokens, embedding batches 512, and rerank with 1024 context. i'll produce a small spreadsheet showing latency vs cost for hosted vs dedicated with quantized models.
[04:40] Dana: how do you handle fallback when capacity is constrained? our product wants graceful degradation to a cheaper model but not to leak PII.
[04:52] Priya: we have smart routing. policy-based fallback to compatible model variants and region fallback, plus prefix/KV cache. note on PII — you can set routing policies to avoid sending certain accounts to hosted or to enforce Private deployments for those accounts.
[05:12] Laila: we need guarantee that PII won't be routed out of our VPC. that's non-negotiable.
[05:22] Priya: understood. for pilot accounts that carry regulated data we'll recommend Private or Dedicated on your project with explicit egress disabled.
[05:32] Ethan: pricing — can you walk through the high-level splits? we need ranges to propose internally.
[05:40] Janelle: offer one: 15% referral + 10% reseller markup on hosted. Dedicated gets a larger share because of ops overhead; example split 20% referral + 15% reseller margin. these are starting points — we'll iterate.
[05:58] Dana: is that standard? our benchmarks with other vendors like CloudServe Inc. were simpler, flat referral 18% but opaque overages.
[06:12] Priya: we're trying to be transparent — we share token usage analytics and route-level cost breakdown in the console so you can reconcile. competitive note, aetherai tends to bundle and hide unit costs which customers dislike.
[06:30] Tom: technical Q — does your runtime support KV cache across model variants? we want to ensure reranker latency isn't impacted by cold starts.
[06:42] Marcus: yes — continuous prefix/KV caching. small caveat: cache warming across model variants requires compatible kv schema; otherwise cold starts happen. we'll show an example.
[06:58] [07:00] Speaker 1 (customer whisper): (inaudible)
[07:12] Marcus: also, quantized model options reduce footprint and cost; for rerank workloads you'll probably want int8x4 quantization — lower cost, small accuracy tradeoff. we'll include quality delta numbers.
[07:28] Laila: when you say int8x4, do you have quantization certs and evals for hallucination/regression? we need to avoid regressions for ranking.
[07:40] Marcus: great point. we run evals tied to prompt sets; for pilot we'll run a regression checklist and set alert thresholds for quality drop. we'll share the eval harness.
[07:58] Priya: ok onto timeline — Dana, you said you want to pick three pilot accounts?
[08:06] Dana: yes, preferably one mid-market customer with no regulated data, one enterprise with EU residency needs, and one strategic account that would require private deployment.
[08:20] Ethan: plus a shadow account for our internal metrics.
[08:28] Priya: perfect. so next steps: send pilot account list and we'll scope the configs.
[08:36] Dana: question on reporting — do you provide per-tenant cost attribution and token level detail for reconciliation to our rev ops?
[08:48] Janelle: yes, per-tenant breakdown, token-level cost, and exportable CSVs. there is an add-on retention fee for logs beyond 90 days.
[09:02] Laila: retention beyond 90 days is required for us — we need 7 years. what are options?
[09:12] Priya: we can provide long-term export to your object store or a managed extended retention add-on; i'm flagging this as a security ops conversation.
[09:24] Laila: also need SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[09:30] Marcus: SAML SSO and SCIM supported — auth flows are standard, we integrate with major IDPs.
[09:40] Tom: do you support customer-managed KMS? we have HSM-backed keys in our environment.
[09:46] Priya: yes, we support KMS integrations; for Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS/HSM. for hosted we integrate with cloud KMS and offer customer-managed keys for some tiers.
[09:58] Dana: legal will want to see sample MSA and partner addendum.
[10:04] Priya: we'll attach a partner T&C draft. note: our older partner docs used 'Redwood Inference' and sometimes 'Redwood Serve' in different places; we'll ensure consistency.
[10:16] Dana: haha yes please do.
[10:20] Marcus: quick perf note — for the embedding pipeline, we recommend batching of 512 with async workers, and prefetching. That matches your earlier payload description. Using that we can get cost per 1k embeddings down substantially.
[10:36] Ethan: for the pilot's success metrics — we propose: latency p95 under 200ms hosted, p95 under 120ms dedicated, embedding throughput > 500/sec, and error rate <0.5%.
[10:54] Marcus: sounds reasonable. we'll validate with microbenchmarks.
[11:02] Priya: ok anyone want to raise red flags about the GTM motion or commercials?
[11:08] Dana: only that ClearData needs preferred partner status in co-marketing and lead routing priority. we want that baked into the partner addendum.
[11:18] Janelle: we can offer partner tiering tied to closed revenue — preferenced leads and co-marketing credits at Gold tier. we'll draft the tiers.
[11:30] Laila: last item — pen test window and vulnerability disclosure process. we need to run appsec checks before pilot.
[11:38] Marcus: we support coordinated pen tests; we've done them in prior Dedicated installs with an MOU.
[11:44] Dana: excellent.
[11:48] Priya: recap / next steps: 1) Redwood sends partner pricing + draft T&C and SOC2 pack (Priya/Janelle) by 2026-03-10. 2) Marcus to produce micro-benchmark doc + config examples by 2026-03-12. 3) ClearData to share pilot accounts + PII/residency notes (Dana) by 2026-03-12. 4) Laila to share KMS/HSM + SSO contacts by 2026-03-12. we'll schedule a 60-min kickoff for pilot week of 2026-03-16.
[12:10] Ethan: sounds good — also please include an example runbook for incident escalation and who to call during pilot.
[12:22] Priya: we'll include the runbook.
[12:30] [12:30] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[12:40] Tom: small technical ask — please include an example nginx config for private endpoint peering (we use Istio as well).
[12:48] Marcus: will do, and we'll throw in an Istio-friendly snippet.
[12:58] Dana: any blockers for legal/finance to sign pilot? we need a one-pager on billing flow to show our CFO.
[13:06] Priya: Janelle will add a billing flow one-pager.
[13:14] Janelle: i'll put together the one-pager and a short invoice example.
[13:20] Laila: thank you — we've been burned by surprise egress fees in other pilots. please be explicit.
[13:28] Priya: we'll call out egress and storage line items clearly.
[13:36] Marcus: and for benchmarking i'll include cost per 1k tokens and per 1k embeddings for the two configs.
[13:44] Dana: great. last question — do you have co-branded marketing assets or case study templates we can reuse?
[13:52] Priya: yes, we have a partner playbook with co-brandable decks and a case study template. i'll send the pack.
[14:02] Ethan: ok thanks all — i think this is actionable.
[14:06] Priya: thanks everyone for the clear asks — we'll follow up with materials and set the kickoff.
[14:12] Dana: thanks, talk soon.
